name: Acid (vial)
text: As an action, you can splash the contents of this vial onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw the vial up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the acid as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 acid damage.

name: Alchemist's Fire (flask)
text: This sticky, adhesive fluid ignites when exposed to air. As an action, you can throw this flask up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the alchemist's fire as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can end this damage by using its action to make a DC 10 Dexterity check to extinguish the flames.

name: Alexandrite
text: A transparent dark green gemstone.

name: Amber
text: A transparent watery gold to rich gold gemstone.

name: Amethyst
text: A transparent deep purple gemstone.

name: Antitoxin (vial)
text: A creature that drinks this vial of liquid gains advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour. It confers no benefit to undead or constructs.

name: Aquamarine
text: A transparent pale blue-green gemstone.

name: Assassin's Blood
text: A creature subjected to this poison must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 6 (1d12) poison damage and is poisoned for 24 hours. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and isn't poisoned.

name: Azurite
text: An opaque mottled deep blue gemstone.

name: Backpack
text: A backpack can hold one cubic foot or 30 pounds of gear. You can also strap items, such as a bedroll or a coil of rope, to the outside of a backpack.

name: Ball Bearing
text: Most commonly found inside a bag of ball bearings.

name: Banded Agate
text: A translucent striped brown, blue, white, or red gemstone.

name: Barrel
text: A barrel can hold 40 gallons of liquid or 4 cubic feet of solids.

name: Basic Poison (vial)
text: You can use the poison in this vial to coat one slashing or piercing weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition. Applying the poison takes an action. A creature hit by the poisoned weapon or ammunition must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take 1d4 poison damage. Once applied, the poison retains potency for 1 minute before drying.

name: Basket
text: A basket holds 2 cubic feet or 40 pounds of gear.

Black Opal
text: A translucent dark green with black mottling and golden flecks gemstone.

name: Black Pearl
text: An opaque pure black gemstone.

name: Black Sapphire
text: A translucent lustrous black with glowing highlights gemstone.

Block and Tackle
text: A set of pulleys with a cable threaded through them and a hook to attach to objects, a block and tackle allows you to hoist up to four times the weight you can normally lift.

name: Bloodstone
text: An opaque dark gray with red flecks gemstone.

name: Blue Quartz
text: A transparent pale blue gemstone.

name: Blue Sapphire
text: A transparent blue-white to medium blue gemstone.

name: Blue Spinel
text: A transparent deep blue gemstone.

name: Book
text: A book might contain poetry, historical accounts, information pertaining to a particular field of lore, diagrams and notes on gnomish contraptions, or just about anything else that can be represented using text or pictures. A book of spells is a spellbook.

Breastplate
text: This armor consists of a fitted metal chest piece worn with supple leather. Although it leaves the legs and arms relatively unprotected, this armor provides good protection for the wearer's vital organs while leaving the wearer relatively unencumbered.

name: Bucket
text: A bucket holds 3 gallons of liquid or ½ cubic foot of solids.

name: Bullseye Lantern
text: A bullseye lantern casts bright light in a 60-foot cone and dim light for an additional 60 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil.

name: Burglar's Pack
text:
Includes:
• a backpack
• a bag of 1,000 ball bearings
• 10 feet of string
• a bell
• 5 candles
• a crowbar
• a hammer
• 10 pitons
• a hooded lantern
• 2 flasks of oil
• 5 days rations
• a tinderbox
• a waterskin
• 50 feet of hempen rope

name: Burnt Othur Fumes
text: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take 10 (3d6) poison damage, and must repeat the saving throw at the start of each of its turns. On each successive failed save, the character takes 3 (1d6) poison damage. After three successful saves, the poison ends.

name: Caltrop
text: As an action, you can spread a single bag of caltrops to cover a 5-foot-square area. Any creature that enters the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or stop moving and take 1 piercing damage. Until the creature regains at least 1 hit point, its walking speed is reduced by 10 feet. A creature moving through the area at half speed doesn't need to make the saving throw.

name: Candle
text: For 1 hour, a candle sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet.

name: Carnelian
text: An opaque orange to red-brown gemstone.

name: Carrion Crawler Mucus
text: This poison must be harvested from a dead or incapacitated carrion crawler. A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. The poisoned creature is paralyzed. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Carved harp of exotic wood with ivory inlay and zircon gems

name: Ceremonial electrum dagger with a black pearl in the pommel
Chain (10 feet)
text: A chain has 10 hit points. It can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength check.

name: Chain Mail
text: Made of interlocking metal rings, chain mail includes a layer of quilted fabric worn underneath the mail to prevent chafing and to cushion the impact of blows. The suit includes gauntlets.

name: Chain Shirt
text: Made of interlocking metal rings, a chain shirt is worn between layers of clothing or leather. This armor offers modest protection to the wearer's upper body and allows the sound of the rings rubbing against one another to be muffled by outer layers.

name: Chalcedony
text: An opaque white gemstone.

name: Chest
text: A chest holds 12 cubic feet or 300 pounds of gear.

name: Chrysoberyl
text: A transparent yellow-green to pale green gemstone.

name: Chrysoprase
text: A translucent green gemstone.

name: Citrine
text: A transparent pale yellow-brown gemstone.

name: Climber's Kit
text: A climber's kit includes special pitons, boot tips, gloves, and a harness. You can use the climber's kit as an action to anchor yourself; when you do, you can't fall more than 25 feet from the point where you anchored yourself, and you can't climb more than 25 feet away from that point without undoing the anchor.

name: Component Pouch
text: A component pouch is a small, watertight leather belt pouch that has compartments to hold all the material components and other special items you need to cast your spells, except for those components that have a specific cost (as indicated in a spell's description).

name: Coral
text: An opaque crimson gemstone.

name: Crossbow Bolt Case
text: This wooden case can hold up to twenty crossbow bolts.

name: Crowbar
text: Using a crowbar grants advantage to Strength checks where the crowbar's leverage can be applied.

name: Diamond
text: A transparent blue-white, canary, pink, brown, or blue gemstone.

name: Diplomat's Pack
text:
Includes:
• a chest
• 2 cases for maps and scrolls
• a set of fine clothes
• a bottle of ink
• an ink pen
• a lamp
• 2 flasks of oil
• 5 sheets of paper
• a vial of perfume
• sealing wax
• soap

name: Disguise Kit
text: This pouch of cosmetics, hair dye, and small props lets you create disguises that change your physical appearance. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to create a visual disguise.

name: Drow Poison
text: This poison is typically made only by the drow, and only in a place far removed from sunlight. A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 hour. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the creature is also unconscious while poisoned in this way. The creature wakes up if it takes damage or if another creature takes an action to shake it awake.

name: Dungeoneer's Pack
text:
Includes:
• a backpack
• a crowbar
• a hammer
• 10 pitons
• 10 torches
• a tinderbox
• 10 days of rations
• a waterskin
• 50 feet of hempen rope

text:

name: Essence of Ether
text: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 8 hours. The poisoned creature is unconscious. The creature wakes up if it takes damage or if another creature takes an action to shake it awake.

name: Exotic Saddle
text: An exotic saddle is required for riding any aquatic or flying mount.

name: Explorer's Pack
text:

• a backpack

• a mess kit

Fire Opal
text: A translucent fiery red gemstone.

name: Fishing Tackle
text: This kit includes a wooden rod, silken line, corkwood bobbers, steel hooks, lead sinkers, velvet lures, and narrow netting.

name: Flask
text: A flask holds 1 pint of liquid.

name: Forgery Kit
text: This small box contains a variety of papers and parchments, pens and inks, seals and sealing wax, gold and silver leaf, and other supplies necessary to create convincing forgeries of physical documents. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to create a physical forgery of a document.

name: Garnet
text: A transparent red, brown-green, or violet gemstone.

name: Glass Bottle
text: A bottle holds 1½ pints of liquid.

Half Plate Armor
text: Half plate consists of shaped metal plates that cover most of the wearer's body. It does not include leg protection beyond simple greaves that are attached with leather straps.

name: Healer's Kit
text: This kit is a leather pouch containing bandages, salves, and splints. The kit has ten uses. As an action, you can expend one use of the kit to stabilize a creature that has 0 hit points, without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

name: Heavy Crossbow
stats: 1d10 piercing · Ammunition (100/400 ft) · Heavy · Loading · Two-handed

name: Hematite
text: An opaque gray-black gemstone.

name: Hempen Rope (50 feet)
text: Rope, whether made of hemp or silk, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

name: Herbalism Kit
text: This kit contains a variety of instruments such as clippers, mortar and pestle, and pouches and vials used by herbalists to create remedies and potions. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to identify or apply herbs. Also, proficiency with this kit is required to create antitoxin and potions of healing.

name: Hide Armor
text: This crude armor consists of thick furs and pelts. It is commonly worn by barbarian tribes, evil humanoids, and other folk who lack access to the tools and materials needed to create better armor.

name: Holy Water (flask)
text:
As an action, you can splash the contents of this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a target creature, treating the holy water as an improvised weapon. If the target is a fiend or undead, it takes 2d6 radiant damage.
A cleric or paladin may create holy water by performing a special ritual. The ritual takes 1 hour to perform, uses 25 gp worth of powdered silver, and requires the caster to expend a 1st-level spell slot.

name: Hooded Lantern
text: A hooded lantern casts bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil. As an action, you can lower the hood, reducing the light to dim light in a 5-foot radius.

name: Hunting Trap
text: When you use your action to set it, this trap forms a saw-toothed steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 piercing damage and stop moving. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet long). A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 piercing damage to the trapped creature.

name: Iron Pot
text: An iron pot holds 1 gallon of liquid.

name: Jacinth
text: A transparent fiery orange gemstone.

name: Jade
text: A translucent light green, deep green, or white gemstone.

name: Jade game board with solid gold playing pieces
Jasper
text: An opaque blue, black, or brown gemstone.

name: Jet
text: An opaque deep black gemstone.

name: Jug
text: A jug holds 1 gallon of liquid.

name: Ladder (10-foot)
text: Ladder (10-foot)

name: Lamp
text: A lamp casts bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil.

name: Lance
text: Special. You have disadvantage when you use a lance to attack a target within 5 feet of you. Also, a lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

name: Lapis Lazuli
text: An opaque light and dark blue with yellow flecks gemstone.

name: Leather Armor
text: The breastplate and shoulder protectors of this armor are made of leather that has been stiffened by being boiled in oil. The rest of the armor is made of softer and more flexible materials.

name: Lock
text: A key is provided with the lock. Without the key, a creature proficient with thieves' tools can pick this lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Your DM may decide that better locks are available for higher prices.

name: Magnifying Glass
text: This lens allows a closer look at small objects. It is also useful as a substitute for flint and steel when starting fires. Lighting a fire with a magnifying glass requires light as bright as sunlight to focus, tinder to ignite, and about 5 minutes for the fire to ignite. A magnifying glass grants advantage on any ability check made to appraise or inspect an item that is small or highly detailed.

name: Malachite
text: An opaque striated light and dark green gemstone.

name: Malice
text: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 hour. The poisoned creature is blinded.

name: Manacles
text: These metal restraints can bind a Small or Medium creature. Escaping the manacles requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity check. Breaking them requires a successful DC 20 Strength check. Each set of manacles comes with one key. Without the key, a creature proficient with thieves' tools can pick the manacles' lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Manacles have 15 hit points.

name: Map or Scroll Case
text: This cylindrical leather case can hold up to ten rolled-up sheets of paper or five rolled-up sheets of parchment.

name: Merchant's Scale
text: A scale includes a small balance, pans, and a suitable assortment of weights up to 2 pounds. With it, you can measure the exact weight of small objects, such as raw precious metals or trade goods, to help determine their worth.

name: Mess Kit
text: This tin box contains a cup and simple cutlery. The box clamps together, and one side can be used as a cooking pan and the other as a plate or shallow bowl.

name: Midnight Tears
text: A creature that ingests this poison suffers no effect until the stroke of midnight. If the poison has not been neutralized before then, the creature must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 31 (9d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Military Saddle
text: A military saddle braces the rider, helping you keep your seat on an active mount in battle. It gives you advantage on any check you make to remain mounted.

name: Moonstone
text: A translucent white with pale blue glow gemstone.

name: Moss Agate
text: A translucent pink or yellow-white with mossy gray or green markings gemstone.

name: Navigator's Tools
text: This set of instruments is used for navigation at sea. Proficiency with navigator's tools lets you chart a ship's course and follow navigation charts. In addition, these tools allow you to add your proficiency bonus to any ability check you make to avoid getting lost at sea.

id: necklace string of small pink pearls|dmg
name: Necklace string of small pink pearls
Net
text: Special. A Large or smaller creature hit by a net is restrained until it is freed. A net has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a DC 10 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it, ending the effect and destroying the net. When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a net, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

name: Obsidian
text: An opaque black gemstone.

id: obsidian statuette with gold fittings and inlay|dmg
name: Obsidian statuette with gold fittings and inlay
Oil (flask)
text: Oil usually comes in a clay flask that holds 1 pint. As an action, you can splash the oil in this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a target creature or object, treating the oil as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target is covered in oil. If the target takes any fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an additional 5 fire damage from the burning oil. You can also pour a flask of oil on the ground to cover a 5-foot-square area, provided that the surface is level. If lit, the oil burns for 2 rounds and deals 5 fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn in the area. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

name: Oil of Taggit
text: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 24 hours. The poisoned creature is unconscious. The creature wakes up if it takes damage.

name: Onyx
text: An opaque black and white banded, or pure black or white gemstone.

name: Opal
text: A translucent pale blue with green and golden mottling gemstone.

name: Padded Armor
text: Padded armor consists of quilted layers of cloth and batting.

name: Pale Tincture
text: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or take 3 (1d6) poison damage and become poisoned. The poisoned creature must repeat the saving throw every 24 hours, taking 3 (1d6) poison damage on a failed save. Until this poison ends, the damage the poison deals can't be healed by any means. After seven successful saving throws, the effect ends and the creature can heal normally.

name: Pearl
text: An opaque lustrous white, yellow, or pink gemstone.

name: Peridot
text: A transparent rich olive green gemstone.

name: Pitcher
text: A pitcher holds 1 gallon of liquid.

name: Plate Armor
text: Plate consists of shaped, interlocking metal plates to cover the entire body. A suit of plate includes gauntlets, heavy leather boots, a visored helmet, and thick layers of padding underneath the armor. Buckles and straps distribute the weight over the body.

id: platinum bracelet set with a sapphire|dmg
name: Platinum bracelet set with a sapphire
Poisoner's Kit
text:
A poisoner's kit includes the vials, chemicals, and other equipment necessary for the creation of poisons. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to craft or use poisons.
Additionally, the Crafting and Harvesting Poison rules require the use of a poisoner's kit.

name: Portable Ram
text: You can use a portable ram to break down doors. When doing so, you gain a +4 bonus on the Strength check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you advantage on this check.

name: Pouch
text: A cloth or leather pouch can hold up to 20 sling bullets or 50 blowgun needles, among other things. A compartmentalized pouch for holding spell components is called a component pouch. A pouch can hold up to ⅕ cubic foot or 6 pounds of gear.

name: Priest's Pack
text:
Includes:
• a backpack
• a blanket
• 10 candles
• a tinderbox
• an alms box
• 2 blocks of incense
• a censer
• vestments
• 2 days of rations
• a waterskin.

name: Purple Worm Poison
text: This poison must be harvested from a dead or incapacitated purple worm. A creature subjected to this poison must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw, taking 42 (12d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Quartz
text: A transparent white, smoky gray, or yellow gemstone.

name: Quiver
text: A quiver can hold up to 20 arrows.

name: Rations (1 day)
text: Rations consist of dry foods suitable for extended travel, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts.

name: Rhodochrosite
text: An opaque light pink gemstone.

name: Ring Mail
text: This armor is leather armor with heavy rings sewn into it. The rings help reinforce the armor against blows from swords and axes. Ring mail is inferior to chain mail, and it's usually worn only by those who can't afford better armor.

name: Ruby
text: A transparent clear red to deep crimson gemstone.

name: Sack
text: A sack can hold up to 1 cubic foot or 30 pounds of gear.

name: Sardonyx
text: An opaque bands of red and white gemstone.

name: Scale Mail
text: This armor consists of a coat and leggings (and perhaps a separate skirt) of leather covered with overlapping pieces of metal, much like the scales of a fish. The suit includes gauntlets.

name: Scholar's Pack
text:
Includes:
• a backpack
• a book of lore
• a bottle of ink
• an ink pen
• 10 sheets of parchment
• a little bag of sand
• a small knife.

name: Serpent Venom
text: This poison must be harvested from a dead or incapacitated giant poisonous snake. A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Shield
text: A shield is made from wood or metal and is carried in one hand. Wielding a shield increases your Armor Class by 2. You can benefit from only one shield at a time.

name: Silk Rope (50 feet)
text: Rope, whether made of hemp or silk, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

Spellbook
text: Essential for wizards, a spellbook is a leather-bound tome with 100 blank vellum pages suitable for recording spells.

name: Spinel
text: A transparent red, red-brown, or deep green gemstone.

name: Splint Armor
text: This armor is made of narrow vertical strips of metal riveted to a backing of leather that is worn over cloth padding. Flexible chain mail protects the joints.

name: Spyglass
text: Objects viewed through a spyglass are magnified to twice their size.

name: Star rose quartz
text: A translucent rosy stone with white star-shaped center gemstone.

name: Star Ruby
text: A translucent ruby with white star-shaped center gemstone.

name: Star Sapphire
text: A translucent blue sapphire with white star-shaped center gemstone.

name: Studded Leather Armor
text: Made from tough but flexible leather, studded leather is reinforced with close-set rivets or spikes.

name: Tankard
text: A tankard holds 1 pint of liquid.

name: Thieves' Tools
text: This set of tools includes a small file, a set of lock picks, a small mirror mounted on a metal handle, a set of narrow-bladed scissors, and a pair of pliers. Proficiency with these tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to disarm traps or open locks.

name: Tiger Eye
text: A translucent brown with golden center gemstone.

name: Tinderbox
text: This small container holds flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a torch—or anything else with abundant, exposed fuel—takes an action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

name: Topaz
text: A transparent golden yellow gemstone.

name: Torch
text: A torch burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a burning torch and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.

name: Torpor
text: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 4d6 hours. The poisoned creature is incapacitated.

name: Tourmaline
text: A transparent pale green, blue, brown, or red gemstone.

name: Trinket
text:
When you make your character, you can roll once on the Trinkets table to gain a trinket, a simple item lightly touched by mystery. The DM might also use this table. It can help stock a room in a dungeon or fill a creatures pockets.
